text:
Jordan Park: hey folks, trying to accept the GitHub org invite but I get an error: 'Organization requires 2FA/SSO' even though I enabled 2FA on my personal account. invite was to jordan.park@gmail.com :confused:

onboarding-bot: Welcome to Redwood! Quick tip: if you have multiple GitHub accounts, accept using the account tied to the invite email. If that doesn't work, ping people-ops so we can reissue.

Maria Chen: @Jordan welcome :wave: Can you DM me your preferred work email? Also try logging out of all other GitHub accounts and accept in a private window. Sometimes cookie/session mixups cause this.

Jordan Park: DM sent. I logged out and retried in an incognito window — still blocks with the same 2FA/SSO message. I have an older github.com account with the same username though.

Ben Ortiz: Hey @Jordan — from infra side org enforces SSO + 2FA. Common case: your personal account has 2FA but not linked to the company SSO. Can you paste your GitHub username here (or DM)? I'll check the pending invite state.

Jordan Park: sure — username is jordanpark. When I hit accept it briefly goes to github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/sso and then errors.

Ben Ortiz: I see a pending invite to jordan.park@gmail.com and also a conflicting personal account that isn't linked to your work email. I can clear the old pending invite and reissue to your work address. Maria — can you resend to jordan@redwood.com and mark it for SSO?

Maria Chen: Done — re-sent invite to jordan@redwood.com and flagged for SSO enforcement. Jordan, try accepting now. If it still fails, add your work email to your personal GitHub account (Settings -> Emails -> Add email) and verify it, then accept. That usually resolves the 'account mismatch' flow.

Jordan Park: Accepted! It prompted me to authenticate via SSO and then asked to approve organization access. After that I see a note saying I need to request access to some private repos (eg. infra-deploy).

Samir Patel: Once you've completed SSO and the invite shows as accepted, I (or @Ben) will add you to the infra and dev-platform teams which grant repo permissions. @Ben can you confirm when you add?

Ben Ortiz: Added Jordan to teams: infra, dev-platform. Also quick SSH tip — generate an SSH key and paste the public key into GitHub so pushes work: 

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "jordan@redwood.com"
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | pbcopy  # or copy manually
```

Add that pubkey in https://github.com/settings/keys.

Jordan Park: Thanks — I added the key and restarted the agent. `git push` was failing earlier (permission denied publickey) but now it's green. Appreciate the quick help everyone :thumbsup:

onboarding-bot: If anything else comes up with access, open a ticket in #help or DM people-ops. Welcome aboard again! :tada:
